2. The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.92 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B,
323 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Bawar, District-Mainpuri after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 22.9.2022 passed by learned Sessions Judge,
Mainpuri.
3. In the present case, applicant's wife died otherwise than under normal circumstances, within two years and two months of her marriage.
According to postmortem report, immediate cause of death was 'Asphyxia' due to ante mortem hanging.

sentences.text: 4. Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of applicant has submitted that before marriage due to an accident, applicant became 40 percent disabled with his leg and this was the reason that his wife was not happy.
She was staying at her parents house for the last two months, where she committed suicide.
5. A Dying Declaration was recovered, wherein she has not levelled any allegation in regard to any cruelty committed in regard to demand of dowry.

He has also placed reliance upon a Supreme Court's judgment in Bhagwan Das Vs. Kartar Singh & Ors, (2008) 1 SCC (Cri) 664, that mere harassment of wife by her husband or in-laws due to disputes or differences may not attract Section 306 I.P.C. read with Section 107 I.P.C. and that if there is no dowry demand soon before the death of wife, it would not attract Section 304-B I.P.C.
6.

sentences.text: Learned Senior Counsel further placed reliance upon a Supreme Court's judgment in M. Mohan Vs. State represented by the Deputy Superintendent of Police (2011) 3 SCC 626.
He further submitted that out of their wedlock a girl child aged about two years was born who is presently staying with her grand parents.

He lastly submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 31.5.2022, there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial and the applicant undertakes that if enlarged on bail, he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.
He lastly submitted that till date not a single witness has been examined.

7. Learned counsel for the complainant as well as learned A.G.A. have opposed the bail application by submitting that deceased died otherwise under other than normal circumstances within two years of her marriage.
She has specifically stated in her dying declaration that her in-laws and his husband used to assault her.
They also submitted that victim has narrated her ordeal of cruelty in regard to the demand of dowry to the complainant and she suffered assault as many as 75 times.
She was so much harassed that she was forced to live at her parental house for the last two months.
There are specific allegations against the applicant for committing cruelty in regard to demand of dowry.
8.LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

sentences.text: In the present case, deceased died otherwise other than under normal circumstances, within a short period of two years of her marriage.
Out of their wedlock, a girl child aged about 2 years was born who is presently residing along with her grand parents.
A dying declaration has been collected during investigation which indicates that she was harassed by her in-laws and applicant used to assault her.
She was so much harassed that due to physical cruelty she had no other option but to commit suicide.

10.There is merit in the argument of learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant that in the dying declaration prima-facie there is no allegation in regard to any demand of dowry by applicant or his family members.

However, statement of brother of deceased is specific in regard to the allegations of demand of dowry by the applicant and his family members who has stated that her sister suffered cruelty many times in regard to demand of dowry.
11. That deceased has narrated her ordeal to the complainant many times.

Even in his presence, her sister was assaulted by the applicant and she was thrown away from her matrimonial house along with her minor daughter of one and a half years, therefore, this evidence cannot be ignored.

Though prima-facie there is no averment in regard to committing cruelty in regard to demand of dowry in dying declaration, still evidence of her brother appears to be cogent to make out a strong prima-facie case against the applicant.
12. Judgments relied on by the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant are not helpful to the applicant at this stage.
13. Accordingly, bail application is rejected.
